transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get this greenlight meeting started. We have an international airline looking to license the concert documentary for their in-flight entertainment system. The draft package proposes a worldwide, twelve-month, non-exclusive license using the current picture and delivery master. Before I can sign off, I need each of you — rights, music, and post-production — to report any approval conditions or concerns. Let's start with rights.

transcript.text: I reviewed the executed performer agreements yesterday, and there are several issues. The agreements only permit licensing in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom — not worldwide as the buyer's draft proposes. The maximum term is six months, not twelve. And critically, the agreements require a written rights amendment before we can proceed to delivery. So we cannot approve this deal as drafted; the territory and term need to be renegotiated, and an amendment must be executed before delivery.

transcript.text: I need to flag a music clearance issue. I checked the publisher's clearance ledger this morning and confirmed that the current cut's use of the song 'Afterglow Avenue' lacks the synchronization clearance required for airline distribution. The cleared replacement is 'Night Transit,' and I have not yet updated the music cue sheet because the final territory and term were still unsettled. So even if the territory and term get renegotiated, we'll need to swap that cue and update the cue sheet before delivery.

transcript.text: I completed the airline's ingest test with the delivery vendor today. The required master is 1080p SDR video with stereo Lt/Rt audio and English SDH captions as a sidecar VTT file. Our current 4K master uses a different audio and caption package, and I have not yet issued the revised export order while the licensing terms remain pending. So I have a post-production approval condition: we cannot deliver on the current master as the draft package proposes — a new export conforming to the airline's spec must be ordered and completed before delivery.
